answer_1.quote: Natural language watermarking uses text as the carrier for the watermark by imperceptibly modifying semantics and/or syntactic features.

answer_2.quote: For payload, we compute bits per word (BPW). For robustness, we compute the bit error (BER) of the extracted message. We also measure the quality of the watermarked text by comparing it with the original cover text.

answer_4.quote: We collected human annotations of the watermarked texts through ClickWorker and disclosed the responses may be used for research purposes.
answer_4.guideline: Part 1 consisted of rating the fluency of each sentence including the original cover text. Fluency ∆ was computed by subtracting the fluency of the watermarked sample from the original one. Part 2 consisted of rating how much semantics is maintained given the reference sentence (cover text).
